prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (max 500 words)

Economy, tax, and finance
- £250bn National Transformation Fund over 10 years for infrastructure and industrial renewal; missions include 60% zero/renewable energy by 2030 and 3% of GDP on R&D.
- National Investment Bank and regional development banks to expand SME lending; stronger ring‑fence between retail and investment banking; curb branch closures.
- Crack down on tax avoidance; no income tax rise below £80k, and no rises in personal NICs or VAT; higher taxes for top earners and large corporations; restore small profits corporation tax rate.
- Balance day‑to‑day budget within five years under a Fiscal Credibility Rule; debt to fall by end of Parliament; strengthen the OBR.

Infrastructure and industry
- Complete HS2 to Scotland and link with “Crossrail of the North”; build Crossrail 2, new Brighton Main Line; nationwide rail electrification; reopen some branch lines.
- Universal superfast broadband by 2022; expand free public Wi‑Fi; improve 4G/5G coverage; plan for 300 Mbps ultrafast rollout.
- Use procurement to drive high standards on tax, pay, training, environment, and prompt payment; encourage stakeholder governance and curb excessive pay.

Ownership and utilities
- Expand co‑operatives; employee “right to own” on company sale; insource public services.
- Return rail, energy networks, water and postal services to public ownership over time.

Energy and climate
- Temporary household energy price cap; major home insulation; support renewables, tidal lagoons, CCS; maintain nuclear; North Sea transition strategy; ban fracking.
- New Clean Air Act; deposit‑return schemes; protect habitats; plant 1m trees; restrict neonicotinoids.

Brexit, immigration, and trade
- Prioritise jobs and standards; seek benefits of Single Market/Customs Union; guarantee rights for EU nationals and reciprocity; avoid no‑deal; protect Ireland border; replace EU funds.
- End freedom of movement; introduce needs‑based migration system; end indefinite detention; tackle labour exploitation; restore Migrant Impact Fund.
- Transparent trade policy; defend standards and public services; support SMEs’ exporting; strong human‑rights conditions in trade.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: expanded early years and childcare; fund Sure Start; restore school funding; reduce class sizes; free primary meals; review testing.
- Free lifelong FE; restore EMA; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; raise apprenticeship quality and completions.

Work and social security
- Day‑one rights for all workers; ban zero‑hours contracts; Living Wage ≥£10 by 2020; sectoral bargaining; end tribunal fees; stronger equality protections; address bogus self‑employment.
- Triple lock on state pension; protect bus passes and winter fuel; fair pension age review.
- Reverse key cuts; reform Universal Credit; disability assessment overhaul; raise ESA (WRAG) and Carer’s Allowance; incorporate UNCRPD.

Housing
- Build 1m+ homes, including 100k social homes annually; empower councils; new towns; higher standards and insulation.
- Three‑year tenancies as norm; cap rent increases; ban letting fees; improve standards; reform leasehold; suspend Right to Buy without like‑for‑like replacement; end bedroom tax; plan to end rough sleeping.

Health and care
- >£30bn extra NHS funding over Parliament; scrap pay cap; restore bursaries; meet waiting‑time standards; end extensive privatisation; free hospital parking.
- Ring‑fence mental health budgets; end out‑of‑area placements; school counselling.
- Foundations for a National Care Service; £8bn more for social care this Parliament; ethical care standards; longer‑term funding cap and reforms.

Safety, justice, and transport
- 10,000 more police; commissioner for tackling domestic and sexual violence; review Prevent; 500 more border guards; 3,000 more firefighters.
- Restore key legal aid; 3,000 more prison officers; end probation/ prison privatisation focus; rehabilitation plans.
- Public ownership of rail; fare caps; municipal bus powers; major rail investments; cycling/walking strategy; taxi/PHV reform; airport capacity subject to strict tests.

Culture, media, sport
- £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; arts pupil premium; protect public service broadcasters; complete Leveson; support media plurality; fan representation in sports; fair ticketing.

Constitution, equality, foreign, defence, development
- Constitutional Convention; extend FOI to outsourced providers; votes at 16; further devolution.
- Strengthen equality enforcement and pay gap reporting.
- Human‑rights‑led foreign policy; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales linked to IHL breaches pending investigation.
- Defence review; spend ≥2% GDP; renew nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; bolster veterans’ support.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; SDG strategy; action on tax havens; refugee plan.
